correctness.rationale: For 2x2 A=I-J=[[a,-c],[-c,d]] symmetric positive definite with c>0, (I-sA)^2 has diagonal terms positive and offdiagonal sc(2-s(a+d)); hence it maps R_+² into itself iff 0<=s<=2/(a+d). With SqS3 s=||Ax||/||A²x||, positive x arbitrarily close to the Perron eigenvector may generate a signed subdominant mode when J has nonzero second eigenvalue. Exact witness J=[[1/2,1/4],[1/4,1/2]], x=(11/10,9/10), s=4sqrt(19729)/181, final J(I-sA)^2x has second coordinate (3769-27sqrt(19729))/3620<0. Independently rederived radical by exact algebra; never inferred all A from finite witnesses.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge original exact orthant feasibility frontier and positive-input counterexample for raw unsafeguarded SqS3. Varadhan–Roland provide the step formula and generic safeguard/globalization; their full accessible pages discuss parameter failures but do not derive the 2D fixed-s matrix entry condition s<=2/tr A or the radical positive-input witness. The result is not claimed for safeguarded methods.
residual_risks: Uninspected later pages 13-19 of the 2008 paper or obscure SQUAREM implementation notes might contain stronger cone-invariance bounds.
Positivity statement excludes gSqS3 safeguarding, clipping and nonsymmetric/nondiagonalizable operators.

value.rationale: Sharp feasibility barrier for a commonly used fixed-point accelerator, with a robust tiny two-dimensional counterexample under a strictly positive contractive base map. It motivates step safeguarding and distinguishes feasible base iteration from feasible extrapolation. Does not criticize or override safeguarded gSqS3.
